title: HECTOR: Historical Economic Commodities: Terminologies, Ontologies & Rates
description:
An open Linked Data vocabulary of historical traded commodities, the units they were measured and packed in, and the customs rates charged on them. Every record gathers the spellings the sources use, links to the Getty Art & Architecture Thesaurus and Wikidata where an equivalent exists, and is published as JSON-LD (with Turtle and RDF/XML) aligned with Linked Art. Its first content comes from the London customs accounts (1380–1560) and the English Books of Rates of 1507, 1545 and 1558, in Stuart Jenks's transcriptions.

Developed within the project Unlocking Upcycled Medieval Data: North Sea Networks, People, and Commodities in the London Customs Accounts 1380–1560, funded by the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC, grant AH/Z507179/1) and the Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft (DFG, project number 547507634) under the AHRC–DFG bilateral scheme.

Persistent URIs: https://w3id.org/hector/. Data CC BY 4.0; code MIT. Contributor roles (CRediT) and full credits: CREDITS.md.
